name: Belize
summary: A will is free, but a court can order maintenance for dependants out of the estate (Wills Act, Cap. 203, Part II). There is no fixed share for children. Belize is a common-law country with trusts and, I believe, a private-foundation statute, but it is not in the Hague Trusts Convention; those two points need confirming.
family_claims: The Wills Act (Cap. 203) has an Inheritance (Family Provision) part giving the court power to order maintenance for dependants out of a testator's estate (s. 35 and following); the tests and time limit were not read.
foreign_law_note: Common-law rule (not confirmed in a Belizean statute here): movables by the law of domicile, land by the law of its location. No right to choose the law of nationality was found.
trust_note: Belize has an own trust statute for local and international trusts (the Trusts Act, Cap. 202; the 1992 international trusts regime is widely cited) and a Private Foundations Act 2010; neither text was read here, so the entries rest on general knowledge and are flagged. Not a party to the Hague Trusts Convention. Foreign-trust tax treatment was not sourced.
open_questions: Trusts Act and Private Foundations Act 2010 were not read; domestic_trusts and private_foundations rest on general knowledge. Confirm the Act numbers and any firewall provision for heirship claims.
Family provision tests, class of applicants and time limit in Cap. 203 Part II were not read.
